title: 첫 모음 세 개: 아, 이, 으 소리 내기
objective: You can read 아, 이 and 으 aloud with the right mouth shape and write each vowel with ㅇ in the right place.
summary: Learn the three basic vowels ㅏ, ㅣ and ㅡ, their mouth shapes, and how to read them with a silent ㅇ.

task.title: Read, shape and write
task.line: Use the letter table and the mouth-shape notes on page 1 to answer each small question.

words.exampleMeaning: Oh, this child! (said when a child is being naughty)

letters.sound: [a] — drop your jaw, open your mouth wide. Built from person (ㅣ) + heaven (ㆍ, a dot to the right)
[i] — spread your lips in a smile, tongue forward. Built from person (ㅣ), a person standing up
[ɯ] — lips flat, teeth almost closed, tongue pulled back. Built from earth (ㅡ), the flat ground
letters.as: like 'oo' in 'good', with lips not rounded

letters.sound: ㅇ before a vowel is silent: 아 [a], 이 [i], 으 [ɯ]
letters.as: a placeholder, like a silent letter. Tall vowels (ㅏ, ㅣ) go to the right of ㅇ (아, 이); flat vowels (ㅡ) go under ㅇ (으)

exercises: Does the vowel go to the right of ㅇ or under ㅇ?: ① ㅡ ② ㅏ ③ ㅣ
Which vowel matches the mouth shape? Write ㅏ, ㅣ or ㅡ: ① lips flat, teeth almost closed, tongue pulled back ② jaw dropped, mouth wide open ③ lips spread in a smile, tongue pushed forward
Which basic shapes make each vowel? Use heaven (ㆍ), earth (ㅡ) and person (ㅣ): ① ㅣ ② ㅏ ③ ㅡ
Write it in Hangul, adding a silent ㅇ: ① eu ② i ③ a-eu
answers: ① under ㅇ (으) ② to the right of ㅇ (아) ③ to the right of ㅇ (이)
① ㅡ ② ㅏ ③ ㅣ
① person (ㅣ) ② person (ㅣ) + heaven (ㆍ) ③ earth (ㅡ)
① 으 ② 이 ③ 아으
